ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Above the horizontal ground there are perpendicular uniform electric and magnetic fields; the direction of the uniform electric field is vertically downward, and the direction of the uniform magnetic field is horizontally inward. Now a positively charged metal ball is thrown horizontally from point M with initial velocity $v_0$. When the ball lands, its velocity is $v_1$, and its flight time in the air is $t_1$. If the magnetic field is removed while all other conditions remain unchanged, then when the ball lands its velocity is $v_2$, and its flight time in the air is $t_2$. Air resistance on the ball can be neglected. Then regarding the comparison of the magnitudes of $v_1$ and $v_2$, $t_1$ and $t_2$, which of the following judgments is correct? ( )
ready1_open_rewrite.title: Relationship of landing speeds
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Above a horizontal ground there exists a uniform electric field vertically downward and a uniform magnetic field horizontally inward. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the small ball starts from point M at a certain height above the horizontal ground, with initial speed v0 horizontally to the right; the ground is the same horizontal plane; electric field E is marked as vertically downward; magnetic field B is represented by crosses, with direction horizontally inward. The problem statement says that the small ball is positively charged, the two initial speeds and starting positions are the same, after removing the magnetic field the other conditions remain unchanged, and air resistance is ignored. Reasoning: To compare the landing speeds, the work-energy theorem can be used. The small ball falls from point M to the same horizontal ground, and the vertical descent height is the same. Gravity is vertically downward, and its work is related only to the descent height; the electric field force on the positively charged small ball is also vertically downward, and its work is likewise related only to the descent height. Therefore, the work done by gravity and the electric field force is the same in the two cases. When there is a magnetic field, the Lorentz force is always perpendicular to the instantaneous velocity, so the magnetic field force does no work. The initial kinetic energies in the two cases are the same, and the total work is the same, so the final kinetic energies are the same, and the landing speeds are the same.

method.method_draft: 采用功能关系/能量法。先从图中确认小球从同一高度 M 点水平抛出，最终落到同一水平地面；电场方向竖直向下，磁场方向水平向里。再从题干读取：小球带正电，初速度均为 v0，撤去磁场前后其他条件不变，忽略空气阻力。比较两种情形的末速度时，只需看动能变化：重力和电场力都竖直向下，做功只与竖直下落高度有关，两次相同；磁场存在时洛伦兹力始终垂直于瞬时速度，不做功。因此两次从出发到着地的总做功相同，初动能也相同，末动能相同，所以着地速率相等，得 v1=v2。
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中小球从离水平地面一定高度的 M 点出发，初速度 v0 水平向右；地面是同一水平面；电场 E 标注为竖直向下；磁场 B 用叉号表示，方向水平向里。题干说明小球带正电，两次初速度和出发位置相同，撤去磁场后其他条件不变，且忽略空气阻力。推理：比较着地速率可用动能定理。小球从 M 点落到同一水平地面，竖直下降高度相同。重力竖直向下，做功只与下降高度有关；电场力对正电小球也竖直向下，做功同样只与下降高度有关。因此两次重力和电场力做功相同。有磁场时，洛伦兹力始终垂直于瞬时速度，所以磁场力不做功。两次初动能相同，总做功相同，所以末动能相同，着地速率相同。
method.answer_match_reason: The predicted answer states exactly the same relationship as the standard answer: v_1 = v_2.
